before.supportingExcerpt: Assay card for spatial transcriptomics (a reading guide, not a score). Measures and how: RNA with coordinates, by preparing a section, capturing or probing RNA, sequencing or imaging, decoding, registering positions and reporting the assignment rules. Input and tissue cost: protocol-compatible frozen or fixed sections; sectioning and molecular preparation consume allocated material, some workflows alter or destroy the assayed section, and re-scoring existing data consumes no new tissue. Output and units: gene counts per spot, bin or assigned cell, and decoded molecule coordinates, often in micrometres, with physical dimensions, normalisation and observed-versus-imputed labels kept. Thresholds: assay-specific gene or probe coverage, capture and decoding quality, background and segmentation criteria; no universal high-expression or neighbourhood cutoff. Failure modes: poor RNA, incomplete probe coverage, low capture, image-registration errors, inaccurate segmentation, spillover and unsuitable reference models. Limits: no automatic single-cell identity, complete transcriptome, whole-tumour representation, proven interaction or clinical selection rule. Validation tier: many workflows are research methods, so check analytical and intended-use validation for the exact assay and model; resolution claims and regulatory status are separate questions.

before.supportingExcerpt: Stoeck 2014 identified NOTCH1 or NOTCH2 rearrangements in six of 66 triple-negative breast cancers. The studied NOTCH1 rearrangements retained gamma-secretase-dependent release of the active intracellular domain, and high-active-NOTCH1 models responded to inhibition in culture and xenografts, including tested paclitaxel combinations. A NOTCH2 fusion encoded an active intracellular product that bypassed the cleavage step and its model resisted that inhibitor. Position alone was not sufficient: a NOTCH1-rearranged line with low active-NOTCH1 signal also resisted. Both the actual active product and model conditions matter. The experiment does not make all activated Notch equivalent, validate a universal staining cutoff or establish a clinical selection rule.

before.supportingExcerpt: Jiang 2013 screened 39 pancreatic cancer lines: the lines sensitive to the tested PORCN inhibitor carried inactivating RNF43 changes. This does not mean every RNF43 variant predicts sensitivity. The reported RNF43-loss models depended on secreted Wnt, whereas a downstream escape from beta-catenin destruction can maintain output despite blocking ligand preparation upstream. before.supportingExcerpt: Assay card for spatial transcriptomics (a reading guide, not a score). Measures and how: RNA with coordinates, by preparing a section, capturing or probing RNA, sequencing or imaging, decoding, registering positions and reporting the assignment rules. Input and tissue cost: protocol-compatible frozen or fixed sections; sectioning and molecular preparation consume allocated material, some workflows alter or destroy the assayed section, and re-scoring existing data consumes no new tissue. Output and units: gene counts per spot, bin or assigned cell, and decoded molecule coordinates, often in micrometres, with physical dimensions, normalisation and observed-versus-imputed labels kept. Thresholds: assay-specific gene or probe coverage, capture and decoding quality, background and segmentation criteria; no universal high-expression or neighbourhood cutoff. Failure modes: poor RNA, incomplete probe coverage, low capture, image-registration errors, inaccurate segmentation, spillover and unsuitable reference models. Limits: no automatic single-cell identity, complete transcriptome, whole-tumour representation, proven interaction or clinical selection rule. Validation tier: many workflows are research methods, so check analytical and intended-use validation for the exact assay and model; resolution claims and regulatory status are separate questions.

before.supportingExcerpt: Jiang 2013 screened 39 pancreatic cancer lines: the lines sensitive to the tested PORCN inhibitor carried inactivating RNF43 changes. Morin's colorectal work linked stabilising beta-catenin changes to this distinction. In a fictional nuclear-beta-catenin culture with such a bypass stipulated, an upstream PORCN block is not expected to remove that particular output. Actual engagement, output and growth still need testing; pathway position is a mechanistic hypothesis, not proof that a drug has no effect through any route.

before.supportingExcerpt: Jiang 2013 screened 39 pancreatic cancer lines: the lines sensitive to the tested PORCN inhibitor carried inactivating RNF43 changes. This does not mean every RNF43 variant predicts sensitivity. The reported RNF43-loss models depended on secreted Wnt, whereas a downstream escape from beta-catenin destruction can maintain output despite blocking ligand preparation upstream. Morin's colorectal work linked stabilising beta-catenin changes to this distinction. In a fictional nuclear-beta-catenin culture with such a bypass stipulated, an upstream PORCN block is not expected to remove that particular output. Actual engagement, output and growth still need testing; pathway position is a mechanistic hypothesis, not proof that a drug has no effect through any route.

before.supportingExcerpt: Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study treated 94 people with advanced solid tumours. AXIN2 RNA decreased in 94 per cent of 52 paired skin-biopsy comparisons and 74 per cent of 35 paired tumour-biopsy comparisons; no RECIST responses were observed. These denominators are paired-sample groups, not response fractions out of all 94 participants. A downstream output change supports a pharmacodynamic effect without directly measuring receptor occupancy, selective growth dependence or tumour shrinkage. Dysgeusia occurred in 50 per cent, illustrating that normal-tissue effects also matter. This trial does not justify transferring a target-output change to benefit or a treatment recommendation.

before.supportingExcerpt: Notch is also used by normal tissues. Van Es and colleagues found that removing the shared Notch transcriptional effector or blocking gamma-secretase converted proliferating intestinal crypt cells into differentiated goblet cells; the study also tested adenomas in Apc-mutant mice. Rangarajan and colleagues found that keratinocyte-specific Notch1 deletion produced epidermal hyperplasia and altered differentiation markers, while their primary-keratinocyte experiments separated growth arrest from differentiation responses. These defined intestinal and skin experiments do not make Notch a tumour-only switch or assign every receptor, tissue and inhibitor the same effect.
before.explanation: Supported source qualification: The conditional crypt and gamma-secretase experiments show a normal intestinal differentiation role; mouse adenoma findings remain separately identified. No universal human dose or response is inferred. Keratinocyte-specific Notch1 deletion and primary-keratinocyte responses establish a defined epidermal differentiation context rather than a tumour-exclusive pathway. Reading is complete raw abstracts and four named OCR spans, not whole papers; inherited claims keep their prior depth.

before.supportingExcerpt: Normal bone also uses Wnt-related signalling. Gong and colleagues linked LRP5 mutations to osteoporosis-pseudoglioma syndrome, found reduced bone mass in carriers, detected LRP5 in osteoblasts and demonstrated canonical Wnt signalling through it in culture. A mutant secreted LRP5 construct reduced bone thickness in mouse calvarial explants. These genetic and experimental findings concern bone accrual; they do not estimate the fracture risk of every Wnt inhibitor. In the WNT974 trial, the authors considered dysgeusia likely to result from on-target Wnt inhibition, but a maximum tolerated dose was not established. Safety findings, pathway-output changes and antitumour benefit remain distinct.
before.explanation: Supported source qualification: Human LRP5 genetics, osteoblast localization, canonical Wnt transduction and mouse calvarial explants support bone accrual roles. These are not a fracture-risk estimate for a drug class. PF-03084014 selection of a lower recommended dose despite comparable target inhibition demonstrates a defined safety/output distinction. Rodon attributes dysgeusia as likely on-target and did not establish an MTD. The teaching qualifies the lesson: it does not prove every event has one normal-tissue mechanism or supply a universal dose ceiling. Reading is complete raw abstracts and four named OCR spans, not whole papers; inherited claims keep their prior depth.

before.supportingExcerpt: Stoeck 2014 identified NOTCH1 or NOTCH2 rearrangements in six of 66 triple-negative breast cancers. The studied NOTCH1 rearrangements retained gamma-secretase-dependent release of the active intracellular domain, and high-active-NOTCH1 models responded to inhibition in culture and xenografts, including tested paclitaxel combinations. Position alone was not sufficient: a NOTCH1-rearranged line with low active-NOTCH1 signal also resisted. Both the actual active product and model conditions matter. The experiment does not make all activated Notch equivalent, validate a universal staining cutoff or establish a clinical selection rule.

before.supportingExcerpt: Assay card for spatial transcriptomics (a reading guide, not a score). Measures and how: RNA with coordinates, by preparing a section, capturing or probing RNA, sequencing or imaging, decoding, registering positions and reporting the assignment rules. Input and tissue cost: protocol-compatible frozen or fixed sections; sectioning and molecular preparation consume allocated material, some workflows alter or destroy the assayed section, and re-scoring existing data consumes no new tissue. Output and units: gene counts per spot, bin or assigned cell, and decoded molecule coordinates, often in micrometres, with physical dimensions, normalisation and observed-versus-imputed labels kept. Thresholds: assay-specific gene or probe coverage, capture and decoding quality, background and segmentation criteria; no universal high-expression or neighbourhood cutoff. Failure modes: poor RNA, incomplete probe coverage, low capture, image-registration errors, inaccurate segmentation, spillover and unsuitable reference models. Limits: no automatic single-cell identity, complete transcriptome, whole-tumour representation, proven interaction or clinical selection rule. Validation tier: many workflows are research methods, so check analytical and intended-use validation for the exact assay and model; resolution claims and regulatory status are separate questions.
before.explanation: Methods retain different physical units and coverage; observed RNA, estimated boundaries, imputation and adjacent-section similarity are distinct. A region/time/block and method-specific validation remain necessary. prior:spatial-transcriptomics: inherited evidence depth; no fresh whole-owner certification

Thresholds: assay-specific gene or probe coverage, capture and decoding quality, background and segmentation criteria; no universal high-expression or neighbourhood cutoff. Failure modes: poor RNA, incomplete probe coverage, low capture, image-registration errors, inaccurate segmentation, spillover and unsuitable reference models. Limits: no automatic single-cell identity, complete transcriptome, whole-tumour representation, proven interaction or clinical selection rule. Validation tier: many workflows are research methods, so check analytical and intended-use validation for the exact assay and model; resolution claims and regulatory status are separate questions.

Input and tissue cost: protocol-compatible frozen or fixed sections; sectioning and molecular preparation consume allocated material, some workflows alter or destroy the assayed section, and re-scoring existing data consumes no new tissue. Output and units: gene counts per spot, bin or assigned cell, and decoded molecule coordinates, often in micrometres, with physical dimensions, normalisation and observed-versus-imputed labels kept. Thresholds: assay-specific gene or probe coverage, capture and decoding quality, background and segmentation criteria; no universal high-expression or neighbourhood cutoff. Failure modes: poor RNA, incomplete probe coverage, low capture, image-registration errors, inaccurate segmentation, spillover and unsuitable reference models. Limits: no automatic single-cell identity, complete transcriptome, whole-tumour representation, proven interaction or clinical selection rule. Validation tier: many workflows are research methods, so check analytical and intended-use validation for the exact assay and model; resolution claims and regulatory status are separate questions.

points.requirement: LC3 carrier flux, delivery to an acidic compartment and actual selected-cargo breakdown are related but distinct measurements requiring suitable controls.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. Sequestosome 1, SQSTM1/p62, is an adaptor whose abundance also depends on expression and other processes, so one p62 snapshot cannot establish blockage.

points.requirement: Autophagy initiation differs from completed lysosomal degradation. A change in mTOR-associated restraint or autophagosome abundance does not establish complete flux.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. PTEN, phosphatase and tensin homolog, removes a phosphate from a PI3K-generated lipid signal. These protein and lipid reactions need their own readouts. Ibrahim 2012 found that PI3K inhibition reduced BRCA1/2 expression and increased PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the BRCA-proficient triple-negative breast cancer models studied. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. Releasing an initiation brake does not establish completed cargo degradation or protective recycling. The two branches can change together without revealing the net survival effect. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.
evidence.explanation: Changing initiation restraint and establishing completed cargo handling are separate outputs. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. More specific branch perturbations and appropriate add-backs can narrow the explanation. Partial rescue can reflect incomplete delivery or restoration as well as additional contributors, so it does not prove a second cause. Place the add-back relative to the blocked step: supplying GGPP after an upstream synthesis block is different from inhibiting the transferase that uses GGPP, which the added substrate cannot simply be assumed to bypass. Include restoration-only and matched controls, verify the restored process and distinguish growth, morphology and death. A genetic perturbation also has its own specificity limits.

points.requirement: More death after a valid perturbation can support a protective role in that system, while less drug-induced death can support a contribution to that response. Neither observation alone identifies a perfectly selective mechanism.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Breast-cancer studies illustrate the conditional direction. Bellare 2021 reported that genetic disruption or chloroquine increased talazoparib sensitivity in the tested HR-proficient cells and xenografts. Arun 2015 found that ATG5 reduction partly reduced olaparib-induced apoptosis in BRCA2-mutant HCC-1428 cells, an oestrogen-receptor-positive line rather than a triple-negative model. These different drugs, models and perturbations do not define one protective or death-promoting label for all tumours. Bellare's 2025 correction replaced representative MCF7 images in Figure 5c as well as a liver-histology image in Figure 6f. The authors stated that replicate-based quantification and interpretation were unchanged; that statement is theirs, not an independent validation of the replacement images.

points.requirement: Cargo delivery, membrane fusion, breakdown and product return are separate steps. Reuse symbols are not proof of extracellular secretion or transport of every product.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A completed macroautophagosome has separate inner and outer membranes, with space between them. When it fuses with a lysosome, the outer membrane joins the lysosomal boundary, while the inner membrane is degraded before enzymes gain access to the enclosed cargo. Itakura and colleagues located syntaxin 17 on completed autophagosomes, and Tsuboyama and colleagues found that loss of ATG conjugation systems markedly delayed inner-membrane degradation even when fusion occurred. A direct-fusion sketch omits intermediate endosomal interactions described in multicellular organisms; it is not the complete route taken by every compartment.
evidence.explanation: Fusion, inner-membrane breakdown and defined product export are separate steps; mammalian amino-acid and yeast evidence do not establish every transported product. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Product return has evidence in defined systems. In leucine-starved cultured human HEK-293T cells, Wyant and colleagues found that SLC38A9 was needed for leucine made by lysosomal protein breakdown to reach the cytosol; the response also depended on the autophagy protein ATG7. Abu-Remaileh and colleagues measured regulated lysosomal amino-acid exchange in mammalian cells. Yeast experiments identified Atg22, Avt3 and Avt4 as partially redundant vacuolar amino-acid exporters. These results support amino-acid recycling in those systems, without establishing transport of every breakdown product, secretion from the cell or guaranteed growth.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. points.requirement: Autophagy initiation differs from completed lysosomal degradation. A change in mTOR-associated restraint or autophagosome abundance does not establish complete flux.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. PTEN, phosphatase and tensin homolog, removes a phosphate from a PI3K-generated lipid signal. These protein and lipid reactions need their own readouts. Ibrahim 2012 found that PI3K inhibition reduced BRCA1/2 expression and increased PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the BRCA-proficient triple-negative breast cancer models studied. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. Releasing an initiation brake does not establish completed cargo degradation or protective recycling. The two branches can change together without revealing the net survival effect. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Breast-cancer studies illustrate the conditional direction. Bellare's 2025 correction replaced representative MCF7 images in Figure 5c as well as a liver-histology image in Figure 6f. points.requirement: Cargo delivery, membrane fusion, breakdown and product return are separate steps. Reuse symbols are not proof of extracellular secretion or transport of every product.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A completed macroautophagosome has separate inner and outer membranes, with space between them. When it fuses with a lysosome, the outer membrane joins the lysosomal boundary, while the inner membrane is degraded before enzymes gain access to the enclosed cargo. Itakura and colleagues located syntaxin 17 on completed autophagosomes, and Tsuboyama and colleagues found that loss of ATG conjugation systems markedly delayed inner-membrane degradation even when fusion occurred. A direct-fusion sketch omits intermediate endosomal interactions described in multicellular organisms; it is not the complete route taken by every compartment.
evidence.explanation: Fusion, inner-membrane breakdown and defined product export are separate steps; mammalian amino-acid and yeast evidence do not establish every transported product. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Product return has evidence in defined systems. A direct-fusion sketch omits intermediate endosomal interactions described in multicellular organisms; it is not the complete route taken by every compartment.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. points.requirement: Autophagy initiation differs from completed lysosomal degradation. A change in mTOR-associated restraint or autophagosome abundance does not establish complete flux.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. PTEN, phosphatase and tensin homolog, removes a phosphate from a PI3K-generated lipid signal. These protein and lipid reactions need their own readouts. Ibrahim 2012 found that PI3K inhibition reduced BRCA1/2 expression and increased PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the BRCA-proficient triple-negative breast cancer models studied. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. Releasing an initiation brake does not establish completed cargo degradation or protective recycling. The two branches can change together without revealing the net survival effect. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Breast-cancer studies illustrate the conditional direction. Bellare's 2025 correction replaced representative MCF7 images in Figure 5c as well as a liver-histology image in Figure 6f. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. PTEN, phosphatase and tensin homolog, removes a phosphate from a PI3K-generated lipid signal. These protein and lipid reactions need their own readouts. Ibrahim 2012 found that PI3K inhibition reduced BRCA1/2 expression and increased PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the BRCA-proficient triple-negative breast cancer models studied. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. Releasing an initiation brake does not establish completed cargo degradation or protective recycling. The two branches can change together without revealing the net survival effect. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The two-window comparison is about scope. A finite plasma aliquot contains extracellular DNA, of which tumour-derived fragments may be one part; breast MRI observes regional, sequence-dependent features rather than individual cancer cells. Contrast enhancement reflects vascular and contrast-delivery behaviour as well as the acquisition protocol; it is not a one-to-one viable-cell count. In the 84-person I-SPY2 MRI pilot, functional tumour volume summed voxels meeting 70% enhancement about two and a half minutes after contrast, inside a manually drawn box around the lesion. points.requirement: Breast MRI measures features in the examined region under its acquisition and interpretation, not a direct count of living cancer cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) assay looks for tumour-associated features in a finite sample of cell-free DNA. evidence.supportingExcerpt: The two-window comparison is about scope. A finite plasma aliquot contains extracellular DNA, of which tumour-derived fragments may be one part; breast MRI observes regional, sequence-dependent features rather than individual cancer cells. Contrast enhancement reflects vascular and contrast-delivery behaviour as well as the acquisition protocol; it is not a one-to-one viable-cell count. In the 84-person I-SPY2 MRI pilot, functional tumour volume summed voxels meeting 70% enhancement about two and a half minutes after contrast, inside a manually drawn box around the lesion. A camera-and-stream analogy illustrates those two sampled views without promising that every tumour sheds DNA. Keep the imaging method visible: mammography uses X-rays, ultrasound uses sound, and PET/CT combines tracer-distribution images with anatomical CT images. A formal response category needs its framework, comparison timepoint and findings outside a selected lesion measurement. None of these measurements is an interchangeable all-body tumour-cell number.

Keep the imaging method visible: mammography uses X-rays, ultrasound uses sound, and PET/CT combines tracer-distribution images with anatomical CT images. evidence.supportingExcerpt: The two-window comparison is about scope. A finite plasma aliquot contains extracellular DNA, of which tumour-derived fragments may be one part; breast MRI observes regional, sequence-dependent features rather than individual cancer cells. points.requirement: Cell-free DNA is outside cells in the sampled fluid; tumour-derived DNA is one possible subset of cell-free DNA, rather than a mutually exclusive material class.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is DNA outside intact cells in a specimen. Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) is the tumour-derived part of the plasma DNA mixture, rather than a different material competing with cfDNA. DNA from non-tumour tissues can contribute much of that mixture, as illustrated by Moss and colleagues' methylation-atlas study. Total extracted DNA is therefore not a tumour measurement. A finite evaluated aliquot can contain no qualifying tumour signal even when disease exists elsewhere.
evidence.explanation: Tumour-derived DNA is a subset of the extracellular DNA mixture, rather than a rival material category. points.requirement: Breast MRI measures features in the examined region under its acquisition and interpretation, not a direct count of living cancer cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) assay looks for tumour-associated features in a finite sample of cell-free DNA. How much tumour DNA reaches the sampled blood varies between lesions, and recovery, background DNA, the features tracked and the assay's detection limit all shape the call. Imaging measures a defined region through a physical signal. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the breast can report contrast enhancement or the volume of enhancing tissue, which is not a direct count of viable cancer cells. The two tests can therefore differ without either being wrong, and neither automatically replaces the other.
evidence.explanation: MRI reports regional, protocol-dependent physical features instead of counting viable cells. evidence.supportingExcerpt: The two-window comparison is about scope. A finite plasma aliquot contains extracellular DNA, of which tumour-derived fragments may be one part; breast MRI observes regional, sequence-dependent features rather than individual cancer cells. Contrast enhancement reflects vascular and contrast-delivery behaviour as well as the acquisition protocol; it is not a one-to-one viable-cell count. In the 84-person I-SPY2 MRI pilot, functional tumour volume summed voxels meeting 70% enhancement about two and a half minutes after contrast, inside a manually drawn box around the lesion. A camera-and-stream analogy illustrates those two sampled views without promising that every tumour sheds DNA. Keep the imaging method visible: mammography uses X-rays, ultrasound uses sound, and PET/CT combines tracer-distribution images with anatomical CT images. A formal response category needs its framework, comparison timepoint and findings outside a selected lesion measurement. None of these measurements is an interchangeable all-body tumour-cell number.
evidence.explanation: MRI reports regional, protocol-dependent physical features instead of counting viable cells. points.requirement: Residual enhancement can have several explanations and does not alone prove viable cancer or prove treatment effect; a near-clean image also has limits.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Four patterns illustrate the reading boundary. A smaller lesion and lower detected blood signal mean that both recorded measures fell in their own units, not that pCR or eradication of distant disease is proved. A residual scan finding with undetected blood leaves viability, treatment effects and other causes unresolved. Detected blood with no suspicious finding in the scanned region does not establish the signal's location, full extent or best intervention. If neither shows qualifying evidence, neither has proved zero microscopic disease or justified omitting indicated treatment. These are interpretation examples, not an action algorithm; disagreement alone does not establish pseudoprogression.
evidence.explanation: The residual-finding pattern leaves viable tumour and treatment/other tissue causes unresolved. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional two-drug table normalises remaining viability to vehicle at 100 per cent: A leaves 70, B leaves 80, and combination examples leave 56 or 30. Both combinations exceed the HSA effect; 56 matches Bliss while 30 exceeds it at that dose pair. A further combination leaving 65 exceeds HSA but not Bliss. Loewe additivity instead needs equivalent-dose information from suitable individual dose-response curves; this one-point table cannot establish it. Report the model, dose-pair pattern, uncertainty and schedule. Interaction relative to a reference does not identify a biological mechanism, tolerable human exposure or a treatment choice.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Two schematic pictures ask different questions. Matched snapshots of DNA-bound PARP1 with a longer or shorter PAR chain illustrate catalytic output; a generic inhibitor in the catalytic pocket does not measure binding duration. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Spatial transcriptomics measures RNA signals while retaining information about where they came from in a tissue section. Sequencing capture and imaging-based detection use different measurement units. A third approach, region-of-interest profiling such as digital spatial profiling, releases oligonucleotide tags only from regions an operator chooses; the method paper describes regions covering 1 to about 5,000 cells and panels of up to 44 proteins, or 1,412 genes with sequencing readout, on formalin-fixed tissue (Merritt and colleagues, 2020), so the result depends on how the regions were selected. The original sequencing-based method placed sections on arrays of positionally barcoded primers and kept two-dimensional position (Ståhl and colleagues, 2016); a capture spot is a positional barcode and can span several cells. MERFISH imaged 100 to 1,000 RNA species chosen by probe design (Chen and colleagues, 2015), a targeted gene set and not every transcript. Assigning molecules to cells depends on estimated cell boundaries: many methods approximate cell positions from nuclear stains, and distinguishing the boundaries of individual cells is challenging and can hamper downstream analysis; Baysor was developed to optimise boundaries from transcript composition and cell morphology (Petukhov and colleagues, 2022). Gene values imputed by aligning single-cell data to a spatial map, as Tangram does (shown in mouse brain; Biancalani and colleagues, 2021), are model outputs and not extra RNA molecules detected by the spatial assay.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Spatial transcriptomics measures RNA signals while retaining information about where they came from in a tissue section. Sequencing capture and imaging-based detection use different measurement units. A third approach, region-of-interest profiling such as digital spatial profiling, releases oligonucleotide tags only from regions an operator chooses; the method paper describes regions covering 1 to about 5,000 cells and panels of up to 44 proteins, or 1,412 genes with sequencing readout, on formalin-fixed tissue (Merritt and colleagues, 2020), so the result depends on how the regions were selected. The original sequencing-based method placed sections on arrays of positionally barcoded primers and kept two-dimensional position (Ståhl and colleagues, 2016); a capture spot is a positional barcode and can span several cells. MERFISH imaged 100 to 1,000 RNA species chosen by probe design (Chen and colleagues, 2015), a targeted gene set and not every transcript. Assigning molecules to cells depends on estimated cell boundaries: many methods approximate cell positions from nuclear stains, and distinguishing the boundaries of individual cells is challenging and can hamper downstream analysis; Baysor was developed to optimise boundaries from transcript composition and cell morphology (Petukhov and colleagues, 2022). Gene values imputed by aligning single-cell data to a spatial map, as Tangram does (shown in mouse brain; Biancalani and colleagues, 2021), are model outputs and not extra RNA molecules detected by the spatial assay.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A tumour specimen can contain malignant, immune, stromal and normal cells. A difference in an aggregate molecular signal can reflect a changed mixture, changed expression within cells or both. That is different from a directly counted cell fraction or a density per sampled area, each of which also needs its denominator and sampled region.

Preparation can change what is recovered. Slyper and colleagues compared single-cell and single-nucleus profiling in matched tumour specimens and found similar cell types at sometimes different proportions. A recovered profile mixture is therefore not automatically the original tissue census. Deconvolution and purity models can help investigate contributions under assumptions; they do not certify the cell of origin of every signal or remove sampling differences.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) is the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) system, with two main classes of peptide-display molecule. Classical class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) has a heavy chain, beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a bound peptide, is found on most nucleated cells, usually displays peptides from proteins made inside the cell and is read by CD8 T cells. Class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) has alpha and beta chains with a bound peptide, is mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells (expression can be induced elsewhere), usually displays proteins processed in vesicles, often acquired from outside, and is read by CD4 T cells. These are common routes, not exclusive lists: cross-presentation puts externally acquired antigen on class I without making it class II, and a CD4 response is not proof of matching class I tumour display. CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors and usual recognition partners, not guarantees of cell function. Structural work shows the T-cell receptor lying across the peptide and HLA together (Garboczi et al., 1996), CD8 contacting the class I alpha2 and alpha3 domains and B2M (Gao et al., 1997) and CD4 engaging a separate class II region (Yin et al., 2012); these constructs do not define universal angles or functions.

HLA alleles are shared across people, and a person inherits a combination that is not necessarily unique. Each person inherits two copies each of HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C, so a cell can display up to six classical class I variants at once. The IPD-IMGT/HLA statistics page read on 9 November 2026 listed 46,146 HLA alleles, 31,311 class I and 14,835 class II (9,457 HLA-A, 11,328 HLA-B and 9,580 HLA-C alleles). Binding predictors estimate whether a peptide can fit a specified allele's groove, but processing, transport, loading and surface expression decide whether it is displayed. Sarkizova et al. (2020) profiled more than 185,000 peptides eluted from 95 mono-allelic cell lines to learn allele-specific motifs and build prediction models; that is allele-level data, not proof of any cell's display. Kaur et al. (2017) showed that HLA-C surface expression varies across individuals in an allele-specific manner, influenced by the structure of the peptide-binding cleft and peptide diversity; Apps and colleagues found lower HLA-C than HLA-A/B in the analysed healthy-donor peripheral blood lymphocytes with the A*02:01/B*44:02/C*05:01 haplotype; the magnitude differed between flow cytometry and mass spectrometry. This is a defined comparison, not a universal hierarchy. The small HLA-C peptide share observed by Schellens and colleagues in four B lymphoblastoid cell lines was also affected by their assignment method, which gave HLA-A/B precedence; it is not a universal biological fraction.

In cancer, class I HLA shows peptides to CD8 T cells and is also the main ligand for inhibitory receptors on natural killer cells, so losing it can hide a tumour from T cells while removing a brake on NK cells. HLA-E and HLA-G are nonclassical and vary little between people; HLA-E presents leader peptides from other class I molecules and binds the NK receptor CD94/NKG2A (Braud et al., 1998, with HLA-E tetramers). Tumours can lose a presenting allele (HLA loss of heterozygosity), alter processing or reduce expression, and allele-specific loss differs from complete loss of conventional class I display; targets on retained alleles may remain possible. Tran et al. (2016) documented a colorectal cancer lesion that progressed after T-cell therapy against mutant KRAS G12D, which had lost the chromosome 6 haplotype encoding the restricting HLA-C*08:02; this shows escape in one patient, not a rate. Typing, protein expression, recovered peptide, recognition and killing are different observations, and a conventional surface-target engager avoids peptide-HLA dependence while a peptide-HLA-directed engager keeps it.

B2M is the light chain of classical class I and does not span the membrane; class II contains no B2M, so CD4 T-cell recognition can remain when B2M is lost. B2M also partners other class I-like molecules: UniProt records heterotrimers with HLA-E, HLA-G, HLA-F and MR1 and lists CD1 interactions, and a B2M mutation caused deficiency of the neonatal Fc receptor FcRn in two siblings (Wani et al., 2006), so complete B2M loss can remove more than classical class I. Loss of one HLA allele can leave other presenting alleles usable, whereas loss of functional B2M impairs many class I targets at once, so several peptides on different alleles are not independent protection. A B2M variant, low RNA, absent surface class I and a blood B2M concentration are different observations: one variant does not show complete functional loss, and blood B2M does not count tumour peptide-HLA complexes. Zaretsky et al. (2016) linked a truncating B2M mutation to lost surface class I in one melanoma relapse after PD-1 blockade, which is a mechanism in that setting, not a frequency. Reduced class I display does not guarantee NK-cell killing, because activating signals are still needed.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) is the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) system, with two main classes of peptide-display molecule. Classical class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) has a heavy chain, beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a bound peptide, is found on most nucleated cells, usually displays peptides from proteins made inside the cell and is read by CD8 T cells. Class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) has alpha and beta chains with a bound peptide, is mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells (expression can be induced elsewhere), usually displays proteins processed in vesicles, often acquired from outside, and is read by CD4 T cells. These are common routes, not exclusive lists: cross-presentation puts externally acquired antigen on class I without making it class II, and a CD4 response is not proof of matching class I tumour display. CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors and usual recognition partners, not guarantees of cell function. Structural work shows the T-cell receptor lying across the peptide and HLA together (Garboczi et al., 1996), CD8 contacting the class I alpha2 and alpha3 domains and B2M (Gao et al., 1997) and CD4 engaging a separate class II region (Yin et al., 2012); these constructs do not define universal angles or functions.

HLA alleles are shared across people, and a person inherits a combination that is not necessarily unique. Each person inherits two copies each of HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C, so a cell can display up to six classical class I variants at once. The IPD-IMGT/HLA statistics page read on 9 November 2026 listed 46,146 HLA alleles, 31,311 class I and 14,835 class II (9,457 HLA-A, 11,328 HLA-B and 9,580 HLA-C alleles). Binding predictors estimate whether a peptide can fit a specified allele's groove, but processing, transport, loading and surface expression decide whether it is displayed. Sarkizova et al. (2020) profiled more than 185,000 peptides eluted from 95 mono-allelic cell lines to learn allele-specific motifs and build prediction models; that is allele-level data, not proof of any cell's display. Kaur et al. (2017) showed that HLA-C surface expression varies across individuals in an allele-specific manner, influenced by the structure of the peptide-binding cleft and peptide diversity; Apps and colleagues found lower HLA-C than HLA-A/B in the analysed healthy-donor peripheral blood lymphocytes with the A*02:01/B*44:02/C*05:01 haplotype; the magnitude differed between flow cytometry and mass spectrometry. This is a defined comparison, not a universal hierarchy. The small HLA-C peptide share observed by Schellens and colleagues in four B lymphoblastoid cell lines was also affected by their assignment method, which gave HLA-A/B precedence; it is not a universal biological fraction.

In cancer, class I HLA shows peptides to CD8 T cells and is also the main ligand for inhibitory receptors on natural killer cells, so losing it can hide a tumour from T cells while removing a brake on NK cells. HLA-E and HLA-G are nonclassical and vary little between people; HLA-E presents leader peptides from other class I molecules and binds the NK receptor CD94/NKG2A (Braud et al., 1998, with HLA-E tetramers). Tumours can lose a presenting allele (HLA loss of heterozygosity), alter processing or reduce expression, and allele-specific loss differs from complete loss of conventional class I display; targets on retained alleles may remain possible. Tran et al. (2016) documented a colorectal cancer lesion that progressed after T-cell therapy against mutant KRAS G12D, which had lost the chromosome 6 haplotype encoding the restricting HLA-C*08:02; this shows escape in one patient, not a rate. Typing, protein expression, recovered peptide, recognition and killing are different observations, and a conventional surface-target engager avoids peptide-HLA dependence while a peptide-HLA-directed engager keeps it.

B2M is the light chain of classical class I and does not span the membrane; class II contains no B2M, so CD4 T-cell recognition can remain when B2M is lost. B2M also partners other class I-like molecules: UniProt records heterotrimers with HLA-E, HLA-G, HLA-F and MR1 and lists CD1 interactions, and a B2M mutation caused deficiency of the neonatal Fc receptor FcRn in two siblings (Wani et al., 2006), so complete B2M loss can remove more than classical class I. Loss of one HLA allele can leave other presenting alleles usable, whereas loss of functional B2M impairs many class I targets at once, so several peptides on different alleles are not independent protection. A B2M variant, low RNA, absent surface class I and a blood B2M concentration are different observations: one variant does not show complete functional loss, and blood B2M does not count tumour peptide-HLA complexes. Zaretsky et al. (2016) linked a truncating B2M mutation to lost surface class I in one melanoma relapse after PD-1 blockade, which is a mechanism in that setting, not a frequency. Reduced class I display does not guarantee NK-cell killing, because activating signals are still needed.
evidence.explanation: Peptide-HLA recognition and natural display are specified; intact-protein detection is not universal immune recognition or killing. evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A conventional alpha-beta T-cell receptor uses paired chains to recognise a peptide-HLA surface. Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) is the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) system, with two main classes of peptide-display molecule. Classical class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) has a heavy chain, beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a bound peptide, is found on most nucleated cells, usually displays peptides from proteins made inside the cell and is read by CD8 T cells. Class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) has alpha and beta chains with a bound peptide, is mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells (expression can be induced elsewhere), usually displays proteins processed in vesicles, often acquired from outside, and is read by CD4 T cells. These are common routes, not exclusive lists: cross-presentation puts externally acquired antigen on class I without making it class II, and a CD4 response is not proof of matching class I tumour display. CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors and usual recognition partners, not guarantees of cell function. Structural work shows the T-cell receptor lying across the peptide and HLA together (Garboczi et al., 1996), CD8 contacting the class I alpha2 and alpha3 domains and B2M (Gao et al., 1997) and CD4 engaging a separate class II region (Yin et al., 2012); these constructs do not define universal angles or functions.

HLA alleles are shared across people, and a person inherits a combination that is not necessarily unique. Each person inherits two copies each of HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C, so a cell can display up to six classical class I variants at once. The IPD-IMGT/HLA statistics page read on 9 November 2026 listed 46,146 HLA alleles, 31,311 class I and 14,835 class II (9,457 HLA-A, 11,328 HLA-B and 9,580 HLA-C alleles). Binding predictors estimate whether a peptide can fit a specified allele's groove, but processing, transport, loading and surface expression decide whether it is displayed. Sarkizova et al. (2020) profiled more than 185,000 peptides eluted from 95 mono-allelic cell lines to learn allele-specific motifs and build prediction models; that is allele-level data, not proof of any cell's display. Kaur et al. (2017) showed that HLA-C surface expression varies across individuals in an allele-specific manner, influenced by the structure of the peptide-binding cleft and peptide diversity; Apps and colleagues found lower HLA-C than HLA-A/B in the analysed healthy-donor peripheral blood lymphocytes with the A*02:01/B*44:02/C*05:01 haplotype; the magnitude differed between flow cytometry and mass spectrometry. This is a defined comparison, not a universal hierarchy. The small HLA-C peptide share observed by Schellens and colleagues in four B lymphoblastoid cell lines was also affected by their assignment method, which gave HLA-A/B precedence; it is not a universal biological fraction.

In cancer, class I HLA shows peptides to CD8 T cells and is also the main ligand for inhibitory receptors on natural killer cells, so losing it can hide a tumour from T cells while removing a brake on NK cells. HLA-E and HLA-G are nonclassical and vary little between people; HLA-E presents leader peptides from other class I molecules and binds the NK receptor CD94/NKG2A (Braud et al., 1998, with HLA-E tetramers). Tumours can lose a presenting allele (HLA loss of heterozygosity), alter processing or reduce expression, and allele-specific loss differs from complete loss of conventional class I display; targets on retained alleles may remain possible. Tran et al. (2016) documented a colorectal cancer lesion that progressed after T-cell therapy against mutant KRAS G12D, which had lost the chromosome 6 haplotype encoding the restricting HLA-C*08:02; this shows escape in one patient, not a rate. Typing, protein expression, recovered peptide, recognition and killing are different observations, and a conventional surface-target engager avoids peptide-HLA dependence while a peptide-HLA-directed engager keeps it.

B2M is the light chain of classical class I and does not span the membrane; class II contains no B2M, so CD4 T-cell recognition can remain when B2M is lost. B2M also partners other class I-like molecules: UniProt records heterotrimers with HLA-E, HLA-G, HLA-F and MR1 and lists CD1 interactions, and a B2M mutation caused deficiency of the neonatal Fc receptor FcRn in two siblings (Wani et al., 2006), so complete B2M loss can remove more than classical class I. Loss of one HLA allele can leave other presenting alleles usable, whereas loss of functional B2M impairs many class I targets at once, so several peptides on different alleles are not independent protection. A B2M variant, low RNA, absent surface class I and a blood B2M concentration are different observations: one variant does not show complete functional loss, and blood B2M does not count tumour peptide-HLA complexes. Zaretsky et al. (2016) linked a truncating B2M mutation to lost surface class I in one melanoma relapse after PD-1 blockade, which is a mechanism in that setting, not a frequency. Reduced class I display does not guarantee NK-cell killing, because activating signals are still needed.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A drug target is a biological molecule or structure that a treatment acts on, and the mechanism of action explains how that action produces an effect. It describes antibodies that mark cancer cells for the immune system, antibodies that stop growth or cause self-destruction directly, and antibodies that carry toxins to cancer cells. These are different jobs, so a shared label of targeted does not make the mechanisms interchangeable, and a target that is only an address for delivery need not drive the cancer's growth.

Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) is the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) system, with two main classes of peptide-display molecule. Classical class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) has a heavy chain, beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a bound peptide, is found on most nucleated cells, usually displays peptides from proteins made inside the cell and is read by CD8 T cells. Class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) has alpha and beta chains with a bound peptide, is mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells (expression can be induced elsewhere), usually displays proteins processed in vesicles, often acquired from outside, and is read by CD4 T cells. These are common routes, not exclusive lists: cross-presentation puts externally acquired antigen on class I without making it class II, and a CD4 response is not proof of matching class I tumour display. CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors and usual recognition partners, not guarantees of cell function. Structural work shows the T-cell receptor lying across the peptide and HLA together (Garboczi et al., 1996), CD8 contacting the class I alpha2 and alpha3 domains and B2M (Gao et al., 1997) and CD4 engaging a separate class II region (Yin et al., 2012); these constructs do not define universal angles or functions.

HLA alleles are shared across people, and a person inherits a combination that is not necessarily unique. Each person inherits two copies each of HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C, so a cell can display up to six classical class I variants at once. The IPD-IMGT/HLA statistics page read on 9 November 2026 listed 46,146 HLA alleles, 31,311 class I and 14,835 class II (9,457 HLA-A, 11,328 HLA-B and 9,580 HLA-C alleles). Binding predictors estimate whether a peptide can fit a specified allele's groove, but processing, transport, loading and surface expression decide whether it is displayed. Sarkizova et al. (2020) profiled more than 185,000 peptides eluted from 95 mono-allelic cell lines to learn allele-specific motifs and build prediction models; that is allele-level data, not proof of any cell's display. Kaur et al. (2017) showed that HLA-C surface expression varies across individuals in an allele-specific manner, influenced by the structure of the peptide-binding cleft and peptide diversity; Apps and colleagues found lower HLA-C than HLA-A/B in the analysed healthy-donor peripheral blood lymphocytes with the A*02:01/B*44:02/C*05:01 haplotype; the magnitude differed between flow cytometry and mass spectrometry. This is a defined comparison, not a universal hierarchy. The small HLA-C peptide share observed by Schellens and colleagues in four B lymphoblastoid cell lines was also affected by their assignment method, which gave HLA-A/B precedence; it is not a universal biological fraction.

In cancer, class I HLA shows peptides to CD8 T cells and is also the main ligand for inhibitory receptors on natural killer cells, so losing it can hide a tumour from T cells while removing a brake on NK cells. HLA-E and HLA-G are nonclassical and vary little between people; HLA-E presents leader peptides from other class I molecules and binds the NK receptor CD94/NKG2A (Braud et al., 1998, with HLA-E tetramers). Tumours can lose a presenting allele (HLA loss of heterozygosity), alter processing or reduce expression, and allele-specific loss differs from complete loss of conventional class I display; targets on retained alleles may remain possible. Tran et al. (2016) documented a colorectal cancer lesion that progressed after T-cell therapy against mutant KRAS G12D, which had lost the chromosome 6 haplotype encoding the restricting HLA-C*08:02; this shows escape in one patient, not a rate. Typing, protein expression, recovered peptide, recognition and killing are different observations, and a conventional surface-target engager avoids peptide-HLA dependence while a peptide-HLA-directed engager keeps it.

B2M is the light chain of classical class I and does not span the membrane; class II contains no B2M, so CD4 T-cell recognition can remain when B2M is lost. B2M also partners other class I-like molecules: UniProt records heterotrimers with HLA-E, HLA-G, HLA-F and MR1 and lists CD1 interactions, and a B2M mutation caused deficiency of the neonatal Fc receptor FcRn in two siblings (Wani et al., 2006), so complete B2M loss can remove more than classical class I. Loss of one HLA allele can leave other presenting alleles usable, whereas loss of functional B2M impairs many class I targets at once, so several peptides on different alleles are not independent protection. A B2M variant, low RNA, absent surface class I and a blood B2M concentration are different observations: one variant does not show complete functional loss, and blood B2M does not count tumour peptide-HLA complexes. Zaretsky et al. (2016) linked a truncating B2M mutation to lost surface class I in one melanoma relapse after PD-1 blockade, which is a mechanism in that setting, not a frequency. Reduced class I display does not guarantee NK-cell killing, because activating signals are still needed.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. points.requirement: PARP catalytic activity/signalling and stabilised DNA-associated protein retention are distinct compound- and assay-dependent observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PARP means poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase, a protein family involved in cellular signalling and repair. PARP1 is one representative. Some inhibitors can also stabilise DNA-associated PARP complexes, often called trapping. A repair-worker analogy separates a reduced call for help from a worker remaining in a doorway; proteins and medicines have no purpose, and the cell has more than one response route.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Rapalogs, PI3K or AKT inhibitors and ATP-site mTOR kinase inhibitors are different interventions. O'Reilly's rapalog study and Harrington's IRS feedback work likewise explain why lower mTORC1 output can coexist with increased upstream signalling. These are measured responses in specified systems, not inevitable behaviour or a universal combination prescription.

points.requirement: PI3K, AKT and mTOR interventions are not interchangeable, and PI3K-alpha/PIK3CA is distinct from PIKFYVE.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Rapalogs, PI3K or AKT inhibitors and ATP-site mTOR kinase inhibitors are different interventions. In Rodrik-Outmezguine's 2011 models, inhibiting both mTOR complexes initially reduced AKT Ser473 and Thr308 phosphorylation, but relief of receptor feedback later restored Thr308 phosphorylation and AKT signalling while Ser473 remained suppressed. A Ser473 result therefore did not measure all AKT activity. O'Reilly's rapalog study and Harrington's IRS feedback work likewise explain why lower mTORC1 output can coexist with increased upstream signalling. These are measured responses in specified systems, not inevitable behaviour or a universal combination prescription.
evidence.explanation: Intervention classes differ; PI3K-alpha/PIK3CA and PIKFYVE are explicitly different targets.
